feat(admininit): offline init admin tail — keyring, deny-all policy/state, epoch last (#47)

* feat(admininit): canonical admin-tail record formats and strict readers (W02.1b I step 10, part 1)

Adds the FMT-PREP-r2 canonical JSON profile (§2.3.1: sorted keys, no whitespace, ASCII-only, lowercase \u escapes, byte-identical to Python json.dumps sort_keys/ensure_ascii) and a strict reader that refuses non-ASCII bytes, duplicate keys (explicit token-level check), lone surrogates, values outside the v1 model and any non-canonical spelling. Typed records and readers for keys/keyring, policy/state (with the default deny-all document) and epoch, plus the server.host_id grammar (§8.2). Tests pin V1-V5 and N1-N15 by length and sha256.

Not yet wired into Init: the subdirectory converge rule, the tail writer, step 10 and the crash cuts follow on this branch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(admininit): admin-tail converge rule and tail writer (W02.1b I step 10, part 2)

FMT-PREP-r2 §2.2 converge rule for keys/ and policy/ (mkdirat EEXIST-ok, no-follow type/owner check, mode restore, dev/ino re-check, fchown+fchmod, per-directory whitelist, fsyncs) and the §2.2.1 tail writer (stale temp unlinkat, O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW temp, fchown/fchmod/fsync on the descriptor, renameat, directory fsync). All steps work on directory descriptors.

P3-FMT7: the mode restore opens the entry O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW, checks dev/ino and changes the mode through /proc/self/fd/<fd>, so it acts on the checked inode and never on a symlink placed at the name later; it also works on a directory left at mode 0000. Tests cover a symlink swap and a directory swap between check and use, a restrictive umask, a supplementary group and the step order.

Still not wired into Init: step 10 orchestration and the C6 crash cuts follow on this branch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(admininit): explicit host_id, admin-area preflight, step 10 tail, pre-epoch check and Status (W02.1b I step 10, part 3)

Init now takes server.host_id as a required parameter, validated against the FMT-PREP-r2 §8.2 grammar in the step-4 preflight before init-intent (HOST_ID_INVALID, not durable, no fallback). Step 4 also checks the top-level admin-area whitelist (ADMIN_AREA_NOT_EMPTY) and that keys/ and policy/, if present, are directories of the init principal (ADMIN_AREA_INVALID). Steps 2 and 3 keep their precedence; init-intent and init-refused are unchanged.

After finish records I, step 10 runs under the held L1/L3 locks: 10a keys/ converge + a new CSPRNG keyring (an earlier attempt's keyring is replaced, never read), 10b policy/ converge + deny-all policy/state for I, the §5.2 pre-write check (ADMIN_TAIL_INVALID: epoch absent, strict re-read of keyring and policy/state, document I, init-intent I, job ledger INIT_MARKER_EMPTY{I}), then 10c epoch durably last. None of these refusals writes init-refused. ReadStatus is a read-only readback under admin.lock shared (new adminlock.AcquireAdminShared) that never returns a key secret.

Tests: host_id grammar and precedence, admin-area preflight, §5.2 refusals, Status, two-process loser-writes-no-tail and status-waits-for-lock, and real-process SIGKILL crash cuts C6a, C6b' (keys umask 077 and 0777, policy), C6b (keyring temp before fchown, state temp before rename), C6c, C6d, C6e, C6f (epoch renamed, killed before the directory fsync) and C6g (ACK lost). A process kill keeps the page cache; physical power loss is not exercised. Existing tests that reran Init after a complete init now remove epoch first (the C6f-absent state) or expect INIT_ALREADY_COMPLETE.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* admininit: refuse escaped CR/LF in secret_b64url and document_b64url

RawURLEncoding.Strict().DecodeString skips CR and LF, and a JSON-escaped CR or LF is canonical JSON, so the strict keyring and policy/state readers (and with them the pre-epoch check) accepted such fields. Decode through decodeB64url, which requires re-encoding to reproduce the field text exactly. Addresses Codex review r4390885139.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(admininit): refuse init when the activation epoch exists (W02.1b I step 3) (#46)

TRUST r4 §3.2 step 3 / D01.3-r6 C.5.7 r5: an <admin>/epoch entry means an
earlier init completed. Init now refuses with INIT_ALREADY_COMPLETE right
after the recorded-refusal check and before the preflight, writing nothing:
no init-intent change, no init-refused, no database, no new installation id.
Any entry under the name counts (file, empty file, symlink, directory).

Init still does not write keys, policy/state or the epoch itself.

commit.message:
feat(adminlock): admin.lock/server.lock protocol and locked offline init (W02.1b I) (#44)

* feat(adminlock): admin.lock/server.lock protocol and locked offline init (W02.1b I)

Implements the RW-C1 lock protocol (D01.3-r6 C.5.8 L1-L3, D01.4-r7 K16) in
internal/adminlock and runs offline init's database phase under it.

- L1: admin.lock is always taken before server.lock.
- L2 AcquireServerStart: admin.lock shared with a bounded wait
  (admin_lock_wait default 15m, 1-60m, outside the range refused),
  WAITING_ADMIN_LOCK logged every 30s, ADMIN_BUSY on timeout; then
  server.lock exclusive without waiting, SERVER_LOCK_HELD if held.
  ReleaseAdmin after classification keeps server.lock. A missing
  admin.lock is reported for the caller to classify.
- L3 AcquireOffline: admin.lock exclusive (created only by init, 0640),
  then server.lock exclusive without waiting, SERVER_RUNNING if held;
  both held until Close.
- admininit.Init takes the L3 locks, refuses database paths outside the
  data root, and holds both locks around ProvisionAndBootstrap. A loser
  returns before either database is opened.

Tests run real second processes (locktest) for the two-PID loser, the
start that waits behind an admin command, and ADMIN_BUSY.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(adminlock): annotate expected gosec findings

G304 on the fixed admin.lock/server.lock names inside the configured
directories, G115 on the fd conversion for flock, and G204 on the test
helper re-executing its own binary, using the repo's #nosec convention.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(adminlock): annotate G302 on server.lock mode and G702 on the test re-exec

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): resolve symlinks before checking data-root containment

Init's check that both database paths are inside the data root was
lexical. With root/link pointing elsewhere, root/link/jobs.db and
root/link/../jobs.db were accepted, and SQLite then created the
database outside the directory that server.lock guards.

Init now resolves symlinks in the data root and in each database path
before the check. An existing path is resolved whole, so a final
symlink is followed and a dangling one is refused. For an absent path
the raw parent is resolved without cleaning, because the kernel
follows a link before "..". Relative paths are made absolute the same
way.

Fixes the independent review finding G-L1 and Codex P1 r4322149017.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(adminlock): locate lock files on the kernel-resolved directory

filepath.Join cleaned the admin area and data root lexically, so a data
root spelled top/link/.. put server.lock in top/ while the kernel opened
the databases under the link target's parent. Init then passed the
containment check and wrote a database that a running server's
server.lock did not guard (pair review G-L1b).

lockPath appends the lock name without cleaning, for admin.lock and
server.lock in both AcquireOffline and AcquireServerStart. Regressions:
offline init and server start through link/.. meet the locks held under
the resolved directory and create no lock file elsewhere; an empty
directory still means the working directory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): pin resolved paths for the lock and every database open

Init resolved the data root and both database paths for its
containment check, but then took server.lock and opened SQLite through
the original paths. A symlink retargeted after the check could leave
server.lock held in one root while SQLite wrote through the link into
another root, where a second process holds a different server.lock.

Init now resolves the data root and both database paths once and uses
those resolved paths for the check, for server.lock and for every
database open in ProvisionAndBootstrap. Regressions retarget a link
right after the check: a data-root link swapped to a root whose
server.lock a running server holds (two processes), and a database
directory link swapped outside the root. The lock and both databases
stay in the checked root.

Fixes Codex P1 r4323139480.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): bind final database entries before SQLite opens them

Codex P1 r4323542522: for an absent database the pinned path is only a
pathname, so a symlink created at the final name after the preflight is
followed by SQLite while Init holds a different root's server.lock.

ProvisionAndBootstrap now holds each database file open from its first
open. An absent file is created empty with O_EXCL, which refuses a
symlink that appeared at the name (an empty regular file is PRISTINE,
so crash resume is unchanged); an existing one must be a regular
non-symlink file. Before and after every SQLite open each held path must
still name its held file, and no sidecar may be anything but a regular
file; otherwise ErrRefused.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): bind each database to the file the preflight inspected

GR-P2-HANDLE-1: a hard link or renamed-in regular file at an absent final name was bound and used, because bind fell back to a plain open on EEXIST and check only compared the path with the held file. ProvisionAndBootstrap now records both database paths (Lstat) before the preflight and requires them unchanged after it. bind creates a file the preflight saw absent with O_CREATE|O_EXCL and refuses EEXIST; a file it saw present is opened with O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and must be a regular file, the same file (os.SameFile) and the same size the preflight saw, so an empty PRISTINE file must still be empty.

P3-AF: a FIFO at the name no longer blocks the open; the held file is refused unless it is a regular file.

Regressions: hard link at the absent ledger and authority names, rename-in over the empty ledger and at the absent authority name, a grown empty file, an authority appearing during the preflight (test hook SetAfterSee), and a FIFO (unix).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): refuse hard-linked databases and keep both bound through the markers

Codex review 6292389810 on fcee75b5 (three P1):

- r4325757882: an existing database with another hard link is refused
  (seeFiles, bind and every check). The other name may sit in another data
  root whose server uses the same file under its own server.lock.
- r4325757906: every database the preflight saw is bound at the first
  durable step, a SCHEMA_ONLY authority that no step opens too, and both
  are checked through the marker commit. An absent one is still created
  only by its own step, so a crash before it leaves it absent.
- r4325757865 (partial): the check after a step runs even when the step
  fails, so a replacement is reported instead of the SQLite error. SQLite
  still opens by path and keeps its sidecars by name, so a file swapped in
  between the check and SQLite's open can be written before the check
  after the step refuses. Closing that window needs a decision on the
  data-root trust model and is left to central.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(admininit): data-root trust for offline init (TRUST r4: I-T1, I-T2, I-G4)

Implements SORI-D01-TRUST-r4 (cf5e2dcd) as accepted with layout L-A,
option (a) and T2 (SORI-TRUST-20261021-R4-IMPLEMENTATION-ADMIT), the
data-root trust decision left open by Codex P1 r4325757865.

I-T1, G1 preflight: the data root and every directory down to a
database must be owned by the init principal, group sori, mode exactly
2770 (setgid, no sticky), with no extended or default ACL (the POSIX
ACL xattrs are parsed). Every ancestor must be owned by root, not
group/other writable and without a write ACL entry. Refusals are
retryable.

I-T2, installation identity: Init keeps <admin>/init-intent (temp,
fsync, rename, dir fsync; 0640). A first init refuses any existing
database or sidecar name durably and writes the intent first. Each
absent database is created O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, its identity tuple (dev,
ino, statx btime, inode generation where readable, uid, gid, mode,
nlink 1) is taken from the descriptor, the path is re-checked, the
coarse clock is waited past the birth time, and the record is made
durable before the descriptor is closed. A resume checks every
recorded file by the full tuple and accepts an unrecorded file only as
the C2 cut (empty, 0660, owner/group, born at or after
intent_created_at, P3-TR6). The database phase binds to the recorded
tuples, and both names and the installation id are checked against the
record afterwards. Identity and binding refusals write init-refused,
so a plain rerun refuses (INIT_REFUSED_STANDS) instead of adopting a
replaced file; I/O, lock, G1 and UNSUPPORTED_FILE_IDENTITY refusals do
not. A filesystem without birth times, and every non-Linux build, is
refused before anything is recorded.

I-G4: databases are created 0660 group sori (fchmod after create, so
the umask does not apply), and sidecars are left 0660 group sori.

The existing binding tests now drive ProvisionAndBootstrap directly,
because Init creates and records both files before the phase. New
Init tests cover G1 modes/owner/group/ACLs/ancestors, pre-existing
files and sidecars, a copied foreign pair, crash cuts C1-C5 and the
steps around them, the C2 birth-time rule, replaced/removed/moved
files, every tuple field, same-owner inode churn with the generation
ignored, the clock-tick wait, the descriptor held until the record is
durable, the phase bound to the record, the step-9 recheck, an
installation id changed in place, and tmpfs refused as unsupported.

Not done here: the explicit discard command (I-exit), the optional
server-start identity row (D-K), a second-uid server open, and
ext4/btrfs/overlay runs. Same-uid in-place writes and held
descriptors stay outside the model (TRUST r4 section 3.5).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* build: pin Go 1.26.10 for GO-2026-6809

crypto/x509 in the Go 1.26.9 standard library carries GO-2026-6809, fixed in 1.26.10. All workflows read go-version-file: go.mod, so the go directive is the only pin. No dependency or code change.

Refs #45

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* admininit: resume the pre-hand-over C2 cut and probe every database filesystem

A crash, or a failed chown or chmod, between the O_EXCL create and the G4 hand-over left an empty owner-only file that the rerun refused durably as unrecorded. The C2 cut now also accepts the owner-only create mode of a file the init principal owns, completes the hand-over on a descriptor checked against the observed identity, and records the 0660 tuple. A file swapped in between is refused durably.

Step 4a probed birth-time support only on the data root. A database directory on a nested mount without birth times let the intent and a database be written before the identity read failed. Each database directory is now probed before the intent or either file is written; the refusal is retryable.

Addresses Codex review comments 4335055244 and 4335055256.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* admininit: hold the recovered C2 file and wait past its birth tick until recorded

A resume that accepted a C2 cut recorded the file's tuple after closing
the descriptor it checked it by (owner-only cut) or without holding one
at all (0660 cut), and without waiting past its birth-time tick. A crash
after that record let same-owner churn reuse the freed inode within the
tick on a filesystem without a usable generation, and a later run adopt
the replacement (Codex P1 4338232085).

recordCut now holds the descriptor through the durable record and waits
past the birth time first, as createAndRecord does, at both cuts; the
held identity is checked against the first look for the 0660 cut too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* adminlock: create server.lock with mode 0660 under any umask

Codex P1 4339947250: os.OpenFile(O_CREATE, 0660) is masked by the umask (0022 leaves 0640), so a server of the sori group under another uid could not reopen server.lock read-write. openServerLock now opens an existing file as it is (mode untouched), and otherwise creates it with O_EXCL and sets 0660 on the open descriptor, only in the process that created it. A name that appears between the two opens is retried a bounded number of times; a dangling symlink is refused instead of followed.

Regressions: umask 022/027/077 on the offline and server-start paths, existing 0600/0640/0644 files keep mode and inode, a concurrently created file is not changed, a dangling symlink is refused and admin.lock released.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* adminlock: publish new lock files with their mode via a linked temporary file

Codex P1 r4340737885: init created admin.lock with O_CREATE, so a restrictive umask (0077) left it 0600 and a sori-group server under another uid could not open it. Codex P2 r4340737900: a crash between the O_EXCL create of server.lock and its fchmod left the name with a umask-masked mode that later opens keep.

Both lock files are now created under a temporary name in the same directory, given their C.5.8 mode (admin.lock 0640, server.lock 0660) on the descriptor, synced, and only then linked to the lock name; the temporary name is always removed. The name therefore never shows a file with another mode. Existing files keep mode and inode, a concurrent creator wins without a mode change, and a dangling symlink at either name is refused.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(adminlock): return temp cleanup failure after losing publication (Codex P2 4342525020)

openLock retried whenever publishLock's error wrapped fs.ErrExist. When the link lost the race and closing or removing the temporary name also failed, the joined error still matched, so the retry opened the winner's lock file and the cleanup failure and the .<name>.tmp-* residue went unreported.

publishLock now reports lost only when the link failed solely because the name exists; a close/remove failure clears it and is returned. Regressions: lost publication + read-only dir (EEXIST link, EACCES remove) for admin.lock by init and server.lock by offline/server start; a non-EEXIST link failure (EPERM) is not retried.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: HeaInSeo <seoyhaein@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(admininit): offline init DB phase — preflight, provisioning, marker bootstrap (W02.1b I) (#43)

* feat(admininit): offline init DB phase — two-DB preflight, schema provisioning, marker bootstrap (W02.1b I)

Adds internal/admininit.ProvisionAndBootstrap (RW-C1 §5.1/§5.1a). It inspects the job ledger and authority databases read-only and refuses before any write unless both are in an init-eligible state. Then it provisions missing known schemas through the version-pinned Open and chooses the installation id (16 CSPRNG bytes, 32 lower hex) only right before the single Init marker transaction. A rerun after a crash at any step resumes, and after the marker commit it reuses the recorded id without calling Init. Locks, keys/policy/epoch, 2PID and S1c startup are out of scope.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): refuse paths that alias one database file (Codex P2)

Compares the two database paths by file identity instead of by Abs string: two existing files by os.SameFile (hard links), two absent files by directory identity plus name (symlinked directories). Adds the hard-link and symlinked-directory refusal cases and a same-name-in-two-directories success case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): compare raw parents so link/.. cannot alias one database (review B1)

When both database files are absent, sameFile compared filepath.Dir of each path. Dir cleans "link/.." lexically, but SQLite opens the raw path and the kernel follows the link before the "..", so <other>/link/../<dir>/jobs.db named the job ledger without being refused. The authority schema was then written into the ledger file before the run failed.

Compare the raw parents (the path up to its last separator, uncleaned) instead. Two new refusal cases, aliasing either path through a symlinked directory and "..", fail on the previous head and pass now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* admininit: refuse SQLite sidecar and case-folded database aliases

Codex P1 r4314292550: when both files are absent, an authority path equal to
the job ledger's -wal (or -shm/-journal), or the reverse, passed the main-file
alias check. Opening the owning database then treated the other one as a stale
sidecar. checkPaths now also compares each main path with the other database's
-wal, -shm and -journal paths.

Codex P2 r4314292577: absent names in one directory are now compared without
case, so jobs.db and JOBS.db are refused before any write. On a case-sensitive
volume this is conservative.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): split raw parents on both Windows separators

Codex P2 r4319772336: rawDir searched only os.PathSeparator, so on Windows C:/data/jobs.db had the parent '.' while C:\data\JOBS.db had C:\data\, and sameFile missed the alias of two absent names. rawDir now scans back for any os.IsPathSeparator byte after the volume name, keeps the non-cleaning behavior, and returns the volume plus '.' when there is no separator. rawDirOf takes the separator rule so the Windows rule is tested on every OS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): refuse Unicode normalization-equivalent absent names

Two absent database names that differ only in Unicode normalization
(a composed "é" and "e" plus a combining accent) preflighted as PRISTINE.
On a normalization-insensitive volume such as default macOS APFS they name
one file, so the authority schema was written and the job ledger then failed
against it after the disk had changed. sameFile now compares absent names
after NFC normalization and case folding, which also covers the SQLite
sidecar aliases. golang.org/x/text becomes a direct dependency at the
version already in the module graph.

Codex P2 r4320419157.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(admininit): refuse Win32 trailing dot/space and full case-fold absent-name aliases

Codex P2 r4321440348: a Win32 path open drops trailing dots and spaces, so absent names such as jobs.db and jobs.db. name one file there, but sameName kept them apart and both preflights reported PRISTINE. Codex P2 r4321440350: strings.EqualFold only applies simple folding, so ß.db and ss.db stayed apart although a default case-insensitive APFS volume can resolve them to one file.

sameName now compares nameKey: trailing '.' and ' ' are dropped, then Unicode canonical caseless matching is applied (NFD, full case folding via golang.org/x/text/cases, NFC). The key is applied on every OS, so these aliases are refused before any write even on a volume that tells them apart, which is conservative. Raw parent identity, symlink and link/.. handling, the existing-file os.SameFile branch, sidecar pair checks and refusal-before-write are unchanged. Full folding now also joins U+FB01 with fi; NFKC-only equivalence is still not joined.

Tests: TestRefusedWritesNothing gains trailing dot/space, sharp s/ss and their -wal/-shm/-journal sidecar alias cases through ProvisionAndBootstrap; TestNormalizationDistinctNames covers ß.db/s.db and jobs.db/.jobs.db as distinct databases; TestSameName adds the rule table rows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: HeaInSeo <seoyhaein@gmail.com>

* feat(jobledger): marker-only Init and read-only InspectInitState (W02.1b I)

RW-C1 overlay r1 §5 row I, jobledger slice (candidate v0.2 §5.1/§5.1a).

- Store.Init's first call is a marker-only bootstrap: one transaction
  requires exactly this version's schema objects, no content rows and no

feat(jobledger): durable Job ledger and policy history (W01.3, E022–E024) (#39)

* feat(jobledger): durable Job ledger and policy history (W01.3, E022–E024)

Add the jobledger package: the J1 single-writer SQLite/WAL ledger for
Jobs, eligibility history and prepared publications (Sori-SM v1.3 W01.3,
D01.2/D01.3 accepted design).

- Atomic acceptance boundary: one IMMEDIATE transaction fences the
  admin-control Guard, classifies (namespace, key, meaning) by D01.2
  B.2.3 (N0/N1/N2/N3/N4/N4H/N5/N6/N7/N8) and, for a new key, writes the
  key -> job_id -> domain operation key mapping with the dispatchable
  Job. Replays return the same Job; a changed meaning is a conflict.
- Jobs keep phase, durable cancel intent, an at-most-once RevisionID and
  a write-once terminal receipt, with record-version CAS.
- Resource block/unblock with an append-only actor/operation/resource
  audit history (data-side evidence; current-policy authority stays in
  admin-control, W09).
- PreparedPublication (one descriptor/mapping per prepared_id, never
  overwritten) and PhysicalBinding INTENT -> ATTACHED_READY; pending
  bindings are never selected.
- Store marker (restore_state, store_active_epoch, store_cut_seq),
  cut absorb/snapshot, restore marker with nonce, and activation, so a
  restored store is read-only and post-cut keys are RECONCILE_HOLD.
- Every mutation appends to a hash-chained ledger (VerifyLedger).

Cross-process tests (re-exec'd child processes) cover E022 cancel
intent across restart, E023 policy history across restart, and E024
prepared/binding reopen, kill before/after the acceptance COMMIT,
concurrent first acceptance, and cut/restore/activation classification
with a replaced old-epoch writer.

Not in scope: admin-control area and sori-admin, namespace token MAC,
gRPC surface, key tombstones/namespace retirement (W02.A, W09).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(jobledger): never resume a cancelled Job; cover ledger seq in the chain

Codex review on 0585142:
- r4243524083: RequestCancel keeps HOLD, and HOLD -> RUNNING was still
  allowed, so a reconciler could resume a cancelled Job. Advance now
  refuses RUNNING/QUEUED for a Job with cancel intent.
- r4243524085: the chain digest excluded seq and VerifyLedger did not
  check contiguity, so renumbering a row verified. The digest now covers
  seq, appendLedger writes it explicitly, and VerifyLedger requires
  seq 1, 2, 3, ...

New tests TestCancelInHoldIsNotResumed and renumber/drop cases in
TestLedgerTamperDetected fail on 0585142 and pass now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(jobledger): reject a ledger whose newest rows were lost

VerifyLedger only checked that rows are contiguous from 1 and chained, so losing the highest rows left a valid prefix and passed (Codex P2 r4243714642). Each append now records seq:digest of the new head in ledger_meta in the same transaction; ledgerHead (LedgerHead, appends, Snapshot) and VerifyLedger refuse with ErrLedgerIntegrity when the last row is not that recorded head. Snapshot verifies the copy's whole chain before returning cut evidence. VerifyCut checks the ledger against a Cut kept outside the store, which also catches a rewrite that moved the recorded head back.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* jobledger: read ledger head and chain in one snapshot

ledgerHead read the last row and ledger_meta.ledger_head in two autocommit statements, so an append committed between them made a healthy store report ErrLedgerIntegrity (GR-P2-HEADREAD). LedgerHead now reads both in one statement; VerifyLedger and VerifyCut read the chain, the recorded head and the cut row in one statement. TestLedgerReadsDuringConcurrentAppend reads from the writer's handle and a second handle during 150 appends.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* jobledger: let a held job with cancel intent record committed success

RequestCancel keeps HOLD, and the cancel-intent check blocks the route through RUNNING, so a held job whose effect had already committed could not record an accurate SUCCEEDED receipt. Allow HOLD -> SUCCEEDED (as CANCEL_REQUESTED already does) and keep the no-resume ban on RUNNING/QUEUED. Addresses Codex review r4270744597.

Regression: HOLD -> cancel -> committed SUCCEEDED keeps the accepted RevisionID and cancel intent, writes the terminal receipt, refuses RUNNING/QUEUED before and any transition or cancel after, and a same-key replay returns the same terminal job.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
acquisition/sqlitecheckpoint: bound Open by one deadline (#37)

Open retried on SQLITE_BUSY until a 10 s budget passed, but each attempt ran with a fixed 10 s busy timeout and one more attempt could start after the budget was spent, so Open could block for close to 20 s under a held write lock. SQLite's busy timeout also applies per lock wait, so connecting (WAL conversion) and init's BEGIN IMMEDIATE could each wait the full time.

All attempts now share one deadline. No attempt starts after it, the busy timeout is capped at the time left when connecting and recomputed before init, init's context carries the deadline, and the busy timeout is set back to 10 s after a successful init. This mirrors the authority/sqlitestore fix from #35.

Fixes #36

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(sqlitestore): retry first-open SQLITE_BUSY and refuse transient paths (#34) (#35)

* fix(sqlitestore): retry first-open SQLITE_BUSY and refuse transient paths (#34)

Port the two W01.2 fixes from acquisition/sqlitecheckpoint (#33) to the
W01.1 authority adapter:

- Open sets the driver's _busy_timeout (applied before any _pragma) and
  retries the whole open+init step only on SQLITE_BUSY within the same
  10 s budget. A process that loses the race to WAL-convert a new
  database file could fail at once with SQLITE_BUSY; the busy handler is
  not always consulted there.
- Open refuses "" and ":memory:" with ErrTransientPath instead of
  returning a non-durable database.

Tests: TestCrossProcessConcurrentOpenOfNewDatabase (two child PIDs race
Open on 8 fresh files, then one accept yields one Revision) and
TestOpenRejectsTransientPaths.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sqlitestore): keep Open within its busy budget (PR #35 review)

Codex P2 r4242808573: after repeated immediate SQLITE_BUSY the loop could
start one more attempt past the deadline, and that attempt could wait the
full 10 s busy timeout, so Open could block for ~20 s.

No attempt now starts once the budget is spent, and each attempt's
_busy_timeout is capped at the budget left. After init succeeds the
connection's busy_timeout is set back to 10 s for the store's own
transactions; the pool keeps that single connection.

Tests: TestOpenReturnsWithinBusyBudget (another connection holds the
write lock; with a 300 ms budget Open returns in ~0.3 s instead of 10 s)
and TestOpenRestoresFullBusyTimeout.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sqlitestore): one Open deadline across connect and init (PR #35 review)

SQLite's busy timeout bounds each lock wait, not the connection, so an
attempt whose WAL conversion spent most of the budget could wait a full
budget again in init's BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Open now passes one deadline to
each attempt, and the attempt recomputes the busy timeout from it after
connecting and before init; init's context also carries the deadline.

TestOpenDeadlineSpansConnectAndInit makes connecting spend 0.8 s of a 1 s
budget and then takes the write lock before init. Open returns in about
1.0 s; without the recompute it took 1.80 s (a context deadline alone
does not end a busy wait).

commit.message:
authority: SQLite/WAL durable authority.Store adapter (W01.1, E016–E018) (#30)

* authority: SQLite/WAL durable authority.Store adapter (W01.1 slice1)

Add authority/sqlitestore, the J1 durable single-writer local profile
(SQLite/WAL on host-local disk). Every mutation runs in one BEGIN
IMMEDIATE transaction committed with synchronous=FULL before the result
is returned. It reuses the MemoryStore semantics and passes the
backend-neutral authoritytest suite including the Reopen tier. Export
authority.MembersEquivalent so adapters share one equivalence rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* go.mod: add modernc.org/sqlite v1.59.0 for authority/sqlitestore

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authority/sqlitestore: cross-process reopen and concurrent-writer evidence (E016, E017)

The test binary re-executes itself so each writer is a separate OS
process on the same database file. E016: state written by one process
(accept, bind, attach, locator and health change) reads back exactly in
another, and a changed-input retry there conflicts. E017: two processes
released by a file barrier produce one durable result for the same input
and exactly one winner plus a conflict for changed accept/bind/attach.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authority/sqlitestore: commit-boundary fault evidence (E018)

A child process SIGKILLed after its writes but before COMMIT leaves no
acceptance; one killed after COMMIT but before the ACK leaves exactly
the complete acceptance and a later retry of the same request returns
it. An in-process failure at the commit boundary rolls back bind and
attach entirely. Adds test-only commit hooks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authority/sqlitestore: satisfy lint (errcheck, gocognit, gosec G104)

Check the Close error on a failed Open and factor the record lookups
into one lookup helper, which also lowers BindAlias and
AttachRepresentation complexity. No behaviour change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authority/sqlitestore: extract bind target check; wrap long signature

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authority/sqlitestore: escape URI path; probe schema version before DDL

Open built the SQLite file: URI by concatenating the raw path, so a name containing ?, # or % was parsed as DSN parameters, a fragment or an escape (Codex r4238312356). fileURI now percent-encodes the path.

init ran this version's DDL before reading meta.schema_version, so a future schema without the current columns failed with a raw SQLite error instead of ErrSchemaVersion (Codex r4238312361). init now probes sqlite_schema first: DDL runs only on an empty database; an unversioned or other-version database is refused unchanged.

Tests: URI-significant directory names (journal_mode=wal, synchronous=FULL, exact file); future/unversioned/meta-without-version databases refused with schema unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* security: raise Go toolchain to 1.26.9 (sori#31)

go1.25.13 standard library is affected by GO-2026-6603, -6605, -6607,
-6608, -6610, -6611, -6612, -6613 and -6617 (crypto/tls, net/http,
net/textproto), all reachable from existing registry/dataspec code and
fixed in go1.26.9. Go 1.25 has no patched release.

CI setup-go reads go-version-file: go.mod, so this single directive
change moves every workflow to go1.26.9. go mod tidy produced no go.sum
change. govulncheck v1.1.4 (DB 2026-10-08) on ./...: 9 called findings
at go1.25.13, none at go1.26.9.

Refs #31

commit.message:
authority: backend-neutral authority.Store conformance suite (#28)

* authority: backend-neutral authority.Store conformance suite

Add authority/authoritytest with a reusable Harness{New, Reopen} and Run that every Store backend must pass: AcceptRevision idempotency/conflict/concurrent same RequestID, BindAlias append-only history order/idempotency/conflict, AttachRepresentation idempotency/conflict/member equivalence/list order, locator/health updates preserving Revision and Representation identity, and deep-copy fidelity. Reopen cases verify durability and are skipped as NOT IMPLEMENTED when Reopen is nil; MemoryStore runs the suite with Reopen=nil.

Suite self-checks reject deliberately broken stores. No durable adapter, shared staging, GC or J2 storage choice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authoritytest: pin bind alias/asset, cross-revision attach and concurrent attach

Guardrail P2x3 on 6d3ebe5e (test-only):
- B2: same BindRequestID with a different alias or a different asset fails closed; both alias histories unchanged.
- C2: same AttachOperationID on a different RevisionID (identical format/proofs) fails closed; second revision stays representation-empty.
- C4: N=16 concurrent same-op attaches yield one RepresentationID and a list of length 1.
Each case has a matching mutant (alias-blind/asset-blind bind reconcile, revision-blind attach reconcile, duplicating attach) that the suite rejects.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* deps: bump oras.land/oras-go/v2 to v2.6.2 (GO-2026-6499, GO-2026-6497)

Fixes #29. oras-go v2.6.2 requires golang.org/x/sync v0.22.0, so MVS raises it from v0.20.0. go.mod/go.sum only; go mod tidy produces no further change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authoritytest: vary presentation and locators in idempotent retries

Codex review on 1443f723 (P2 x2):
- AcceptRevision/IdempotentRetry now also retries the same RequestID with
  only Manifest.Presentation changed; it must reconcile to the original
  Revision, not ErrRequestConflict.
- Attach retries now carry a locator different from the original attach.
  The retry must reconcile to the one Representation, and must not
  overwrite availability (locators/health) set since the attach.

New mutants, all rejected (and all accepted by the previous suite):
presentation-comparing accept reconcile, locator-comparing attach
reconcile, availability-overwriting attach retry.

Test-only. Product authority package unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authoritytest: assert attach retry returns stored availability

Codex P2 4165030560: after locators=[B]/unhealthy, the idempotent AttachRepresentation retry return itself must carry the stored availability, not the retry request's locatorC/healthy. Adds a mutant that stores correctly but echoes the request availability.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(authoritytest): profile-only retry and reopen reconcile cases

Codex P2 4165089476: AcceptRevision/IdempotentRetry retries a valid external-import request with only AcceptRequest.Profile changed (I4A to unspecified and back) and requires the original Revision. Codex P2 4165089482: Reopen/Revision retries with only Manifest.Presentation changed after reopen. Codex P2 4165089486: Reopen/Representation retries the attach with locatorC after reopen and asserts the returned and stored availability stay locatorB/unhealthy. Five new mutants (profile-strict accept; restored presentation-strict accept; restored locator-strict, availability-resetting and request-echo attach) are rejected; all five pass the previous suite. Test-only; product authority code and dependencies unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(authoritytest): profile, bind-field and cross-revision reconcile after reopen

Codex P2 4166459564/4166459571/4166459580 on e49c9be6. Test-only.

- Reopen/Revision: accept an external-import manifest under each
  profile before reopen; after reopen a profile-only retry must return
  the original Revision.
- Reopen/AliasHistory: after reopen, reusing a BindRequestID with only
  Alias or only AssetID changed must fail with ErrAliasBindingConflict
  and leave both histories unchanged.
- Reopen/Representation: after reopen, reusing the attach operation on
  a second Revision with the same fingerprint must fail with
  ErrAttachConflict, add no relation and keep availability.
- Four new reopen mutants (profile-strict accept, alias-blind and
  asset-blind bind, revision-blind attach); the old suite accepted all
  four. revisionBlindAttach now returns the stored Representation on a
  hit so only its missing RevisionID comparison is wrong.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authoritytest: catch ID reuse after reopen for revisions and representations

Codex 4167021789: Reopen/Revision now requires the next RevisionID to differ from every persisted revision (req-1 and both profiled revisions) and re-reads each of them, so an allocator that reuses an ID and overwrites a record is caught.

Codex 4167021801: Reopen/Representation now commits a fresh attach (attach-2, formatTwo) after reopen and requires a new RepresentationID, both records intact (restored availability unchanged) and list order [rep, fresh].

New mutant 'reopen restores id allocators one behind' is rejected by both cases; the previous reopen.go accepted it. Test-only; product authority code and dependencies are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(authoritytest): full-fingerprint conflicts and conflicting races

Codex P2 4168216406: same RequestID with only builder identity, input lineage or member data format changed must return ErrRequestConflict, before and after reopen. Mutant: reconcile on (AssetID, member digests) only.

Codex P2 4168216413: two Revisions race under one BindRequestID; one side wins, the other gets ErrAliasBindingConflict, history has one event. Mutant: uniqueness on the full binding, not the request id.

Codex P2 4168216422: two formats race under one AttachOperationID; one side wins, the other gets ErrAttachConflict, one representation. Mutant: uniqueness on the relation, not the operation id.

Test-only; product authority package and go.mod/go.sum unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(authoritytest): check the oracle Revision carries the submitted RequestID

Codex P2 4169169814: every sameRevision check used the first accepted Revision as its oracle, so a Store that consistently omits or corrupts Revision.RequestID in both accept responses and reads passed. acceptAs/carriesRequest now require the first Revision to carry the submitted RequestID before it becomes the oracle (accept helper, profile-only retry, concurrent conflicting winner, deep-copy, reopen profiled accepts). Reads stay covered through sameRevision against that checked oracle.

Mutants: accept and read omit / corrupt RequestID, plain and across reopen. The old suite accepted all 12 mutant/case pairs.

Test-only; product authority package and go.mod/go.sum unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(authoritytest): check the oracle BindEvent and Representation against their requests

Codex P2 4170035190/4170035198: a store that consistently rewrites
BindEvent.BindRequestID or a logical binding field, or Representation.AssetID
or RevisionID, on writes and reads alike passed the suite, because the first
returned value became the oracle for every later comparison. bindAs/attachAs
now require the first BindEvent to record the submitted BindRequest and the
first Representation to carry the submitted op, asset, revision and format
before a case uses them. New rewriting mutants are rejected by every case
that uses those oracles, with and without reopen.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(authoritytest): check oracle fingerprints against the facade-supplied ones

A Store could reconcile on the fingerprint the facade supplies yet
consistently expose a blank or corrupted Revision.Fingerprint or
Representation.Fingerprint from accept/attach and reads alike; the first
result then became the oracle and the suite certified it. acceptAs,
attachAs and the concurrent-conflict winner now compare the returned
fingerprint with the one the production facade supplies for the same
request, derived through a recording probe Store independent of the Store
under test. Blank/corrupt fingerprint mutants for revisions and
representations (including across reopen) must now fail certification.

Addresses Codex review 4170842800 and 4170842807.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(authoritytest): ground revision oracles in the request and cover two-member paths

Codex 4171185221: acceptedAs now also requires the first Revision to
record the submitted AssetID and full Manifest (members compared as a
set), so a Store that consistently corrupts asset ownership or an
external-import manifest field can no longer pass by being
self-consistent. attachMatches checks the returned member proofs too.

Codex 4171185233: new AcceptRevision/MultiMember and
AttachRepresentation/MultiMember cases round-trip a two-member Revision
and Representation, accept reordered retries as the same operation,
and require a change confined to the second member to conflict (accept,
attach) or fail member equivalence (new attach).

Nine new mutants (asset/source rewrite, member truncation, first-member
reconcile/equivalence, order-strict reconcile) are each rejected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(authoritytest): pin second-member and second-proof rewrites

Adds two length-preserving broken-store mutants to TestSuiteRejectsBrokenStores: one rewrites only the second Revision member's proof digest on accept and read, the other only the second Representation member proof on attach, get and list. AcceptRevision/MultiMember and AttachRepresentation/MultiMember must reject them, so weakening the member-set comparison to a count check no longer survives the committed mutation suite.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(authoritytest): pin multi-member reopen, initial availability, algorithm and role identity

Reopen/MultiMember: a two-member Revision and a Representation carrying both proofs survive a reopen intact, and reordered retries after reopen reconcile to them. Lossy-reopen mutants (first member/proof only, second member/proof rewritten) pass every single-member Reopen case and are rejected only here.

Representation/AvailabilityPreservesIdentity now requires the first attach response to carry the submitted locators and the healthy state. AttachRepresentation/MemberEquivalence refuses the same digest under another algorithm with zero relations. AttachRepresentation/IdempotentRetryAndConflict retries with only the proof roles changed and requires the original Representation.

New broken stores: lossy reopen x4, initial availability dropped, digest-only equivalence, role-strict reconcile, role-echo retry. authoritytest only; authority package unchanged.

Addresses Codex P2 4171705114, 4171705116, 4171705118, 4171705120, 4171705123.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(authoritytest): pin algorithm reconcile and post-reopen member, proof and role identity

Reused attach operation with only the proof algorithm changed must conflict before member equivalence (Codex 4172000740). Reopen/MultiMember now also requires a post-reopen role-only retry to reconcile (4172000743), a second-member-only change under the same RequestID to conflict with the Revision unchanged (4172000744), and a second-proof-only change under the restored attach operation to conflict with the relation unchanged (4172000746). Four broken stores the previous suite accepted are now rejected: algorithm-blind attach reconcile, and restored first-member, first-proof and role-strict reconcile indexes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authoritytest: require algorithm-only conflict after reopen

Reopen/MultiMember now retries the restored attach operation with only a proof algorithm changed and requires ErrAttachConflict with the original relation unchanged. A backend that rebuilds its attach index from semantic keys and digests only passed the suite before (Codex 4176606947); the new restored-index mutant pins it. The other-algorithm literal becomes the proofAlgo2 fixture constant.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authoritytest: algorithm-only acceptance conflict and per-key proof association

Codex 4177013866 / 4177013873 on 23fc9d54 (authoritytest only):

- fingerprintOnlyConflicts (live and after reopen) also reuses req-1
  with only the member proof algorithm changed and requires
  ErrRequestConflict. Killed: algorithmBlindAccept (reconciles on the
  whole manifest except proof algorithms), live and restored.
- attachMultiMember swaps the two digests between m1 and m2, keeping the
  proof set: a fresh operation must fail ErrMemberEquivalence and the
  committed attach-multi must fail ErrAttachConflict; the relation count
  stays 1. Killed: keyBlindEquivalenceAttach and newKeyBlindAttach
  (unordered proof-set comparison).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* authoritytest: swapped proof keys conflict after reopen

Codex P2 r4179704196: Reopen/MultiMember now reuses attach-multi with the existing proofs swapped between semantic keys and requires ErrAttachConflict; the final check keeps exactly one relation with the original identity. New broken store restoreKeyBlindAttach (restored attach index on the unordered proof set) passed the old suite and is now rejected. authority package untouched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

sori: classify replica-local staged absence as retryable (#27)

A STAGED checkpoint records a replica-local staged path. When another
replica resumed it, the missing directory was reported as ErrStagedInvalid
wrapping ErrDigestMismatch (IsFailClosed=true), a false integrity verdict.

A staged directory that does not exist here is now ErrStagedUnavailable:
retryable, not fail-closed. The operation is CAS-reset to PINNED with its
OperationID, fingerprint, subject and PublicationRequestID unchanged, and
the retry re-transfers. A present but wrong or incomplete copy still fails
closed.

Also adds acquisition/checkpointtest, a reusable CheckpointStore conformance
suite. Its logical tier runs on every store; its durability tier runs only
when the harness can reopen the store, so the memory store reports SKIP
there instead of a durability PASS.

commit.message:
SORI-I4A OCI pull-by-digest acquisition (#25)

* SORI-I4A: OCI pull-by-digest acquisition first slice

First bounded I4A reference transport (OCI registry pull-by-digest; not an
OCI-only architecture). New package acquisition:

- Acquisition operation identity (OperationID) + CheckpointStore seam
  (interface + MemoryCheckpointStore reference impl; no DB/topology choice).
  Operation fingerprint excludes endpoint/credential, so mirror/credential
  rotation on retry continues the same operation.
- Manifest digest pinned into the durable operation record before any
  transfer; it is the frozen subject proof. Tags are never authority.
- Stage -> verify -> atomic accept handoff: blobs staged into a temp OCI
  layout via registryutil/ORAS, independently re-verified against the pinned
  digests, atomically renamed; mismatch fails closed. Resumed staged copies
  are re-verified. ACCEPT_PENDING_UNKNOWN makes an unknown acceptance outcome
  explicit; retries reconcile through a publication RequestID minted once
  per operation and kept distinct from the OperationID.

authority: AcceptRequest.Profile (ProfileI4AOCIDigest) requires
ObservedVersion + a well-formed ObservedChecksum only for I4A-produced
ExternalImport. Zero profile keeps the I1M contract; the profile is not
identity-bearing, so existing I1M revisions are not invalidated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(acquisition): keep the CAS winner's staged copy under concurrent attempts

G1: two attempts of one OperationID racing from PINNED shared a fixed staged
path. transfer removed that path and renamed its own copy onto it, so a loser
could replace or delete the copy the winner had already recorded.

- Each attempt publishes its own staged path (the unique suffix of its tmp
  dir). os.Rename refuses an existing directory, so nothing is replaced.
- The STAGED checkpoint CAS decides which copy is recorded. The loser removes
  its own copy only after a definitive rejection (ErrCheckpointStale or
  ErrOperationConflict). After an ambiguous checkpoint failure the copy is
  kept, because it may be referenced.
- Resume re-verification removes an invalid copy only after the PINNED reset
  is checkpointed.

A crash between publish and checkpoint leaves an unreferenced copy. This slice
does not garbage-collect such orphans.

Tests: TestI4A_ConcurrentSameOperationKeepsWinnerCopy (synchronized two-attempt
race; fails on the previous head) and TestI4A_AmbiguousStagedCheckpointKeepsCopy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(acquisition): reject non-v2 manifests and conflicting duplicate descriptors

Codex P1 x2 on #25 @611718eb:
- parsePinnedManifest now requires schemaVersion == 2; a digest-valid
  document with the image-manifest media type but a missing or other
  schemaVersion fails closed with ErrSubjectInvalid.
- descriptors (config + layers) that share a digest must declare the same
  size. subjectBlobs transfers and verifies a shared digest once, so a later
  inconsistent descriptor was never checked; it is now rejected before
  staging and again on staged re-verification.

Regressions: UnsupportedSchemaVersionFailsClosed (0/1/3),
ConflictingDuplicateDescriptorFailsClosed (layer-layer, config-layer),
ConsistentDuplicateDescriptorAccepted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

SORI-I3P: exact Revision member resolve with authoritative format/cardinality (#24)

* SORI-I3P: exact Revision member resolve with authoritative format/cardinality

Member gains immutable, identity-bearing DataFormat and Cardinality
declarations (Q2). Acceptance requires both; they are never inferred from
Presentation, locators or health. Representation member proofs still prove
content equivalence only.

Add ResolveRevisionMember(ctx, assetID, revID, semanticKey), pinned to the
exact Revision. It fails closed with typed ErrRevisionNotFound (unknown or
cross-asset revision) and the new ErrMemberNotFound (Q4), and returns the
attached representations unfiltered.

Focused TestI3P regressions cover the exact resolve, unknown and
cross-asset revisions, a missing member, an unhealthy representation, a
pinned read across an alias rebind, zero representations, declaration
validation and declaration identity.

Eligibility (Q1), transport/public DTO (Q3) and a durable backend (Q5)
are out of scope.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* SORI-I3P: reject declaration-bearing representation proofs (fail-closed)

AttachRequest.MemberProofs reuses Member, so after DataFormat/Cardinality
became authoritative Member fields a proof could carry a contradictory
declaration (e.g. bam/MULTIPLE against a fastq/SINGLE revision) that
equivalence ignored and ResolveRevisionMember then returned inside reps.

validateAttachRequest now rejects any proof member with a non-empty
DataFormat or a non-Unspecified Cardinality with ErrInvalidRepresentation.
Proofs are proof-only; the accepted Revision's Member stays the sole
declaration authority.

Tests: proof-only proofMember fixture for representation requests;
TestI3P_10 (conflicting/matching/unknown declarations rejected, nothing
attached) and TestI3P_11 (resolved representation carries no declarations).

commit.message:
fix(referrer): record typed semantic artifactType on OCI referrers (P-A, Alt A) (#23)

Both referrer producer paths passed the generic
`application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json` as the ORAS PackManifest artifactType
argument, so toolspec/dataspec/toolprofile/security referrers were not identifiable by
their exact semantic kind at the OCI top-level artifactType (only in config.mediaType).
ORAS v2.6.1 packManifestV1_1 records that argument verbatim as manifest.ArtifactType,
which the referrers API surfaces for discovery/?artifactType= filtering. Central
GR-SIGNATURE-REFERRER-GAP-20260816 F-4.

Alt A: record each referrer's existing semantic media type as the top-level
artifactType, keeping the same value in config.mediaType (dual-record). No new
artifactType namespace.

- pushSpecReferrer: pass mediaType (ToolSpec/DataSpec/ToolProfile/SecurityScan).
- pushDataSpecManifest: pass MediaTypeDataSpec (second DataSpec path, parity).

config.mediaType and the config payload bytes are unchanged, so LEGACY referrers
(generic top-level artifactType + semantic config.mediaType) remain valid historical
objects, recognizable via config.mediaType during migration. No legacy migration/
rewrite/delete here; NodeVault dual-read/consumer honesty is a separate guardrail
packet (GR-NV-REFERRER-SPEC-HONESTY-20260905). Non-referrer primary-artifact
PackManifest paths are untouched. No public Go/proto/RPC change.

Tests: TestReferrer_TypedTopLevelArtifactType (4 kinds: typed top-level artifactType ==
semantic == config.mediaType, referrers-API predecessor descriptor typed, subject
binding intact, config payload bytes unchanged), TestReferrer_ToolSpecVsDataSpecTypedDistinct,
TestPushDataSpecManifest extended (path-2 typed artifactType + primary-artifact
non-referrer regression guard). build/test/-race/vet/gofmt/golangci-lint(0) green.

SORI-I1M: acceptance + minimum semantic manifest spine (embeddable authority) (#21)

* SORI-I1M: acceptance + minimum semantic manifest spine (embeddable authority)

Add an embeddable Sori Asset Authority package (authority/) implementing the
smallest durable spine that can accept one genuinely valid immutable Asset Revision,
per SORI-I1M §§3–10 — without representations, acquisition, Pipeline/DagEdit
integration, lifecycle taxonomy, UI, or any public schema/ID/hash commitment.

- Identity: internal opaque AssetID (distinct from alias/name/version), immutable
  store-assigned RevisionID, durable PublicationOperation RequestID. These are
  internal handles, not a public identifier algorithm or wire schema (§10).
- Minimum Semantic Manifest: typed publication origin; non-empty members with an
  opaque-but-stable semantic key/role + authoritative content-proof reference (reuses
  the chunked CAS digest substrate, §9); origin-required identity-bearing provenance
  (External Import / Derived Asset / Produced Promotion, §6).
- Acceptance evidence + fail-closed validation: structural validity, member closure,
  authoritative proofs, origin-required provenance.
- Accept/reconcile (atomic with the commit, in the Store): same request + same asset
  + same identity-bearing fingerprint → the same Revision; same request + a different
  fingerprint → ErrRequestConflict.
- W2 fingerprint (§5): identity-bearing facts only (asset, origin, order-normalized
  members{key,role,proof}, origin-required provenance; derived includes builder +
  runtime-image + frozen recipe + sorted input lineage). Presentation/discovery
  metadata is excluded, and the fingerprint is internal comparison evidence only —
  never the public Revision-ID/hash.
- W1 alias binding (§4): an operation-identified, append-only alias→Revision history;
  a retry with the same BindRequestID returns the same event (no duplicate history),
  a different binding under the same id is ErrAliasBindingConflict.
- Atomic durability: the Store abstraction commits a Revision all-or-nothing (no DB/
  service/topology commitment, §8); MemoryStore is a reference implementation.

ArtifactMetadata/DatasetMetadata/StableRef and physical OCI push remain
non-authoritative substrate (§9): authority truth exists only after acceptance.

Tests (authority/authority_test.go) cover all ten mandatory acceptance attacks §7:
retry-idempotency, request/proof conflict, derived-builder conflict, alias-binding
idempotency + queryable history, crash-during-commit observability, push-does-not-
infer-acceptance, accept-without-representations, provenance-by-origin (incl.
explicit-unknown external builder + no fabrication), presentation-not-identity-bearing,
and packaging-cannot-substitute-for-authority.

Verification: go build/vet/gofmt clean; make lint 0 (incl depguard); gosec 0;
go test -race ./... all packages ok.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* SORI-I1M: enforce Revision immutability + identity-bearing lineage order (review fixes)

Adversarial review of PR #21 found a P0 and a P1:

P0 (immutability, §8): the accepted Revision shared its Members / InputLineage /
Presentation backing storage with both the caller's AcceptRequest and every
GetRevision return value, so committed authority truth was mutable through those
aliases (a caller reusing its members slice, or any reader mutating a returned
slice, silently rewrote the accepted member set/proof/provenance). MemoryStore now
deep-copies the manifest on commit, on the reconcile-return, and on GetRevision
(cloneManifest/cloneRevision), so an accepted Revision is effectively immutable
across callers.

P1 (fingerprint, §5): input lineage was sorted, collapsing order-distinct derived
lineages ([A,B] vs [B,A]) into the same fingerprint — which could silently merge two
genuinely different derived manifests under one RequestID. Input lineage order is now
treated as identity-bearing (not sorted); providing a canonical order is the caller's
responsibility. Member order remains normalized (duplicate keys are rejected, so
sort-by-key is a total order and member ordering stays non-identity-bearing).

P2 hardening (fail-closed): content-proof digest, member semantic key/role, and each
derived input-lineage entry are now rejected when blank/whitespace-only; BindAlias
rejects binding an alias to a Revision owned by a different asset.

Tests: TestI1M_AcceptedRevisionIsImmutable (mutate caller input + GetRevision result,
assert stored truth unchanged, retry still reconciles),
TestI1M_InputLineageOrderIsIdentityBearing (order-distinct lineage under same request
id conflicts), TestI1M_BindAliasRejectsCrossAsset. Full gate green: make lint 0
(incl depguard), gosec 0, go test -race ./... all packages ok.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fixed-head re-review found two trivial residuals in the touched code:

- P2: cloneManifest guarded the Presentation clone with len>0, so a non-nil EMPTY
  Presentation map was shared with the caller/reader. A map is index-mutable in place,
  so the stored/returned manifest's presentation was still reachable. Clone whenever
  the map is non-nil. (Non-authoritative — excluded from the fingerprint — so it never
  affected identity; closing it completes the immutability guarantee.) Regression:
  TestI1M_EmptyPresentationMapIsIsolated.
- P3: corrected a stale doc comment that claimed input lineage is order-normalized; it
  is order-preserved (identity-bearing), consistent with the P1 fix.

make lint 0 (incl depguard), go test -race ./authority/ ok.

chore: bump Go toolchain to go1.25.13 to clear govulncheck advisories (#19)

Bump the go directive from 1.25.12 to 1.25.13. CI uses setup-go with
go-version-file: go.mod, so this makes CI install go1.25.13, whose
standard library carries the fixes for the govulncheck advisories that
currently block every sori PR. These are the four "called"
(gate-blocking) advisories reported by `make vuln`:

  GO-2026-6218  net/url: quadratic complexity in resolvePath
  GO-2026-6090  crypto/tls: post-handshake message limit
  GO-2026-5972  encoding/asn1: recursion depth guard
  GO-2026-5026  net/http (x/net/idna): reject ASCII-only Punycode labels

All four are stdlib, fixed-by-version in go1.25.13 (the 1.25 line's
backport of the go1.26.6 fixes). No govulncheck exceptions added; the
fix is entirely the toolchain version.

No toolchain directive is added (the repo pins via the go directive).
go.sum is unchanged: the bump adds no new module requirements.

Validated locally with GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.25.13 (local host runs go1.26.5,
so GOTOOLCHAIN reproduces CI's 1.25 stdlib line): go build, go vet,
go test -race all pass; go mod tidy is idempotent; `make vuln` reports
0 vulnerabilities.

Unblocks PR #18.

commit.message:
test: isolate per-chunk digest-mismatch branch, cover push partial-failure (#13)

* test: isolate per-chunk digest-mismatch branch, cover push partial-failure

Two remaining items from #11:

- TestFetch_ChunkDigestMismatch previously only asserted err != nil,
  and used a size-heuristic ("blobs >100 bytes") to pick which blob to
  corrupt. That heuristic isn't reliable: rerunning it after tightening
  the assertions showed it was actually corrupting the OCI image index
  blob, not a chunk blob - failing store initialization before Fetch's
  per-chunk digest loop (fetch.go step 3) ever ran. The old bare
  err != nil assertion couldn't tell the difference, so this test
  never actually proved the per-chunk check works. Fixed by resolving
  the manifest and picking a blob whose MediaType is MediaTypeChunk
  specifically, and strengthened the assertions to check errors.Is
  ErrIntegrity, the per-chunk error-message shape, and (via a Progress
  callback) that no FileDone event was emitted.

- TestPushLocalToRemote_PartialFailureDoesNotCommitManifest: publishes
  a chunked artifact (config + chunk-index + chunk blobs, so multiple
  separate uploads precede the manifest), pushes to a registry that
  lets the first blob upload succeed and drops the connection on the
  second, and asserts the manifest is never written - proving the
  push is all-or-nothing rather than silently completing. Verified
  the mock/test can tell success from failure (a sanity variant
  allowing all uploads through confirms the manifest IS written then).

Addresses two of the remaining items in #11 (a real registry smoke
cycle in CI and skip-tracking annotations remain open there).

* Assert the second blob upload was actually attempted before failing

Review finding: the test's error assertion alone couldn't distinguish
an interrupted second upload from a push that fails before ever
reaching it, so it would pass unchanged even against a broken push
that stops after a single blob.

commit.message:
test: cover push-path auth failure (same class as the fixed CVE) (#12)

* test: cover push-path auth failure (same class as the fixed CVE)

The known CVE fixed in this repo's history was credential-forwarding
on push. Yet every automated auth test that runs in CI exercised only
the fetch path (TestFetchVolumeFromRemote_Unauthorized/_Forbidden) -
the push credential path (PushLocalToRemote -> pushLocalTagToRepository
-> registryutil.NewRepository, which forwards Username/Password) was
covered only by an env-gated integration test skipped in CI, and even
that only exercised valid credentials, never an auth failure.

Add an httptest-based push test mirroring the existing fetch tests:
mock registry returns 401 + WWW-Authenticate on every non-ping request,
assert errors.Is(err, ErrAuth), and assert an Authorization header was
actually sent at some point - proving credentials were forwarded to
the push path, not just that push failed for some unrelated reason.

Addresses the push-auth item of #11 (one of several; push-partial-
failure, a CI smoke-cycle wiring, and skip-tracking annotations remain
open there).

* test: reproduce GO-2026-5882 (cross-host upload-redirect credential leak)

A review bot correctly flagged that TestPushLocalToRemote_Unauthorized
only proves auth headers are forwarded on a same-origin retry - a
check both the vulnerable oras-go v2.6.0 and the fixed v2.6.1 pass
identically, so it provides zero regression protection against the
actual CVE class this package's oras-go pin was bumped to fix.

Looked up the real advisories (govulncheck -show verbose against a
scratch module pinned to v2.6.0): three credential-forwarding CVEs -
GO-2026-5885 (bearer-token realm hijack), GO-2026-5884 (redirect
credential forwarding), GO-2026-5882 (blob-upload Location-header
credential forwarding). GO-2026-5882 is the one on sori's actual push
path: oras-go's blob upload does POST-to-initiate -> 202 Accepted with
a Location header -> PUT to that Location, reusing the POST's
Authorization header. The v2.6.1 fix (repository.go's sameUploadHost
check) rejects the PUT outright if Location points to a different
host than the registry.

Add TestPushLocalToRemote_RejectsCrossHostUploadRedirect: a malicious
registry responds to the upload-initiate POST with a Location on a
different host (an "attacker" test server), and the test asserts the
attacker server receives zero requests - proving oras-go never even
attempts the cross-host PUT, let alone forwards credentials to it.

Verified this test actually distinguishes the two versions: copied the
package to a scratch module, downgraded to oras-go v2.6.0, and
confirmed this new test fails there (attacker server receives the
real PUT with blob content) while the old auth test still passes
unchanged - exactly reproducing the reviewer's point.

---------

ci: automate dependency update pull requests

Matches NodeVault's dependabot.yml — weekly gomod + github-actions
updates, grouped by minor/patch to reduce PR noise. Part of the
cross-repo guardrail standardization sweep (common Baseline A.6).

fix(ci): rename lint job to disambiguate from test.yml's identical 'Run on Ubuntu' check name

Both lint.yml and test.yml used the job display name 'Run on Ubuntu',
producing two check-runs with the identical name on every PR. A
branch ruleset's required status check matches by name only, so
requiring 'Run on Ubuntu' would be satisfiable by either job
succeeding — not a real guarantee that both lint and tests passed.

docs: warn about DataCatalog/RegisterPackagedData deprecation (sori#3)

readme.md, docs/public-api.md, and docs/stable-api-promotion.md still
described DataCatalog/NewDataCatalog/RegisterPackagedData as ordinary
Experimental API with no caveat, even though experimental_registration.go
now carries a Deprecated godoc noting there is no production caller.
Add a matching Deprecated notice to all three docs so readers relying on
them see the same warning as the code.

fix(security): wire lint-security/vuln hard gates into CI, bump oras-go v2.6.1 + go 1.25.12 (#4)

Full CI audit: sori had zero automatic security scanning. gosec and
govulncheck only ran through security-observe.yml (workflow_dispatch
only, never on push/PR). The Makefile already had hard-failing
variants of both (lint-security, vuln — as opposed to the
-observe/soft ones the manual workflow uses) sitting completely
unwired from any CI workflow. Added both as steps in test.yml, right
after the existing test run.

Running vuln for the first time (in actual CI, go1.25.11) surfaced 4
real findings:
- 3x oras.land/oras-go/v2 v2.6.0, all fixed in v2.6.1: GO-2026-5885
  (Bearer token realm hijack can exfiltrate credentials), GO-2026-5884
  (registry redirect credential forwarding), GO-2026-5882 (blob upload
  credential forwarding via unvalidated Location header) — real risk
  for a repo whose entire purpose is OCI registry interaction. Bumped
  (only x/sync moved as its own dependent, no wider cascade).
- GO-2026-5856 (crypto/tls Encrypted Client Hello privacy leak, fixed
  go1.25.12) — go.mod bumped from 1.25.11 to 1.25.12, pure stdlib
  patch, go.sum unaffected.

gosec: 0 issues, so this promotion is net-zero-risk beyond the two
fixes above — nothing else currently reachable starts failing CI.
